analysis:
Examined the complete supplied base/head SetupCommand, both patches and Progress metadata. SetupCommand.swift:166-192 changes an already-installed setup from reporting only to downloading and executing the service installer in plan mode, then optionally reinstalling with derived counts. This expands use of the existing TB-013/T-061 owner-account execution contract (A-019), rather than establishing a new installer-authentication flaw. HTTPS validation, non-root execution, temporary-directory cleanup and signal handling remain present. Fresh setup still checks eligibility and requires confirmation or --yes; added free-space reporting is informational. No supplied change touches plaintext inference, keys, attestation, cache encryption/isolation (T-041), authorization or ledger operations.
Availability interactions require integration: SetupCommand.swift:171 checks a status snapshot, while :191 relies on the external installer to refuse changes if jobs start afterward; :393-396 documents that contract but does not prove its enforcement or omission. Verify the installer’s job fence and no-force arguments to protect running work/payment and TB-012 holds. SandboxSlotChange, SandboxSizingPlan and SandboxInstaller implementations are not supplied: verify bounds, missing-count handling, onlyAdds semantics and exact application of approved counts at :185-205 and :353. These are coverage limits, not findings. The shared confirmation helper retains default-no for existing callers, but the new default-yes call at SetupCommand.swift:214-215 exposes the observed EOF approval issue.

findings.detail: The new default-yes prompt converts readInput() returning nil into an empty answer and therefore approves the change. On an interactive terminal, the owner can press Ctrl-D at the sizing prompt (or the terminal can lose its input) and setup will proceed with installation, including a plan that removes slots. This bypasses the new requirement that slot reductions receive interactive agreement; the noninteractive onlyAdds guard does not apply because interactiveInput was checked earlier. Preserve nil as a distinct result and return false on EOF, accepting the default only for an explicitly submitted empty line.
findings.title: End-of-input is treated as approval for slot changes
